=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh:3766-3799 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Line 3766 (`LAST_FOLLOWUP_BY_FILE["${FOLLOWUP_FILE_KEY}"]="${FOLLOWUP_EXISTING_NUMBER}"`) overwrites the per-file value in index-row order without the `-gt` max guard that the open map at lines 3767-3770 uses, so the closed-predecessor fallback at lines 3793-3799 (`FOLLOWUP_DEPENDS_ON_ANY`) can pick a lower-numbered closed predecessor rather than "the highest closed one" that the README, changelog, agents.d fragment and comment promise.
  WHY: If one file has two closed predecessors listed as #9105 then #9100, the consolidated issue gets `Depends on: #9100`, and `security_dependency_verdict` (scripts/security_dependency.py lines 87-91) releases the hold once #9100 is closed with `ai:merged`, even though #9105 was closed without it; `test_security_audit_consolidated_followup_falls_back_to_highest_closed_predecessor` misses this because its closed predecessors are in different files. Severity disagreement: minimax, openai and z-ai rated MAJOR; anthropic rated NIT, because it only matters when all predecessors are closed and one file has several; the highest (MAJOR→high) is used.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:3478-3481 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The dedupe logic adds the first marker_regex.search(body) match to issue_finding_ids even when that marker sits below the leading marker block.
  WHY: An ai:security issue whose body has prose and then a quoted finding marker, with no leading marker block, is treated as an existing follow-up, so the audit skips filing that finding's follow-up, against the documented rule that markers below the leading block do not count.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:3777-3793 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When several files have open follow-ups (e.g. file_b #9100 and file_c #9105), the consolidated issue depends only on the highest-numbered open predecessor (lines 3790-3791), so merging that one releases the hold while other open predecessors are still unmerged.
  WHY: A consolidated fix can start while another file's open predecessor fix is still in flight, and neither the comment at 3777-3783 nor the agents.d "Depends on." bullet documents this limit (z-ai: a hard limit, because scripts/security_dependency.py:63-68 rejects repeated declarations). Severity: z-ai rated NIT (confidence 3); gemini stated no severity on this finding (confidence 4). anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 treated it as a hardening-only design limit.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:3552-3554 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The tracker line `- Follow-up mode: consolidated ({len(planned_followups)} findings in one issue)` is printed whenever `consolidate_active` is true, even when `planned_followups` is empty and no issue is filed.
  WHY: A consolidated retry where every finding is deduped (the `test_security_audit_consolidated_retry_dedupes_every_leading_marker` scenario) posts "consolidated (0 findings in one issue)" next to "New follow-up issues planned this run: 0", which is contradictory; the impact is on human readers only, since nothing parses the line. All three reviewers rated NIT.
- tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py:N/A | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The recent AI autofix run is said to have introduced regressions in `test_gh_api_write_guard.py`, `test_files_touched_scope_guard.py`, `test_orchestrate_lib.py`, `test_session_start_extract_repo_slug.py`, and `ruff` linting.
  WHY: Gemini says the changes in `scripts/security_audit.sh` caused side effects that make the CI suite fail; it stated no severity. Disagreement: z-ai notes these test files are outside the PR's changed-file set, that no hunk maps to the failures, and that the only completed failed check-run is the external `copilot-pull-request-reviewer` custom-instructions-size error.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "One consolidated follow-up issue per cycle that lists every new finding of that cycle instead of one issue per finding."
  expected_change_site: scripts/security_audit.sh dependency logic
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The single "Depends on" dependency tracks only the highest-numbered predecessor instead of keeping the hold until all open predecessors are closed, which may not meet the "consolidated" intent if the consolidated issue is meant to carry the combined dependency of all its findings (SEVERITY: MAJOR).
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh:line 3766, lines 3793-3799 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `LAST_FOLLOWUP_BY_FILE["${FOLLOWUP_FILE_KEY}"]="${FOLLOWUP_EXISTING_NUMBER}"` is overwritten in `findings` order with no `-gt` comparison (unlike lines 3767-3770), so the closed fallback (`FOLLOWUP_DEPENDS_ON_ANY`) does not pick "the highest closed one" that the README row, changelog fragment, agents.d bullet and comment at 3780-3783 claim. Example: for file_b, #9105 then #9100 gives `Depends on: #9100`.
  WHY: `security_dependency_verdict` (scripts/security_dependency.py lines 87-91) releases the issue if #9100 is closed with `ai:merged`, whatever #9105's state; the new test cannot catch this because its predecessors are in different files. Fix: a separate any-state per-file max map with a `-gt` guard, or reword the docs to say "last-listed closed predecessor".
- HARDENING (2 related items): (1) comment at lines 3777-3783 and the "Depends on." bullet in agents.d/stuck-states-p5b-consolidated-followup.md should note that with open predecessors in several files only the highest-numbered one is depended on; (2) lines 3766 and 3793-3797 should keep a per-file any-state max map, with a `-gt` guard and an update at line 3826, read at line 3793. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh:line 3766, lines 3793-3799 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `LAST_FOLLOWUP_BY_FILE` assignment overwrites unconditionally, while the sibling `LAST_OPEN_FOLLOWUP_BY_FILE` uses a max comparison, so a file with several closed predecessors (e.g. #9100 and #9105) holds the last-processed number, not the highest that agents.d and the README document.
  WHY: The `FOLLOWUP_DEPENDS_ON_ANY` fallback can point at a closed predecessor that is not the highest; if that one is closed with `ai:merged` and the higher one without it, `scripts/security_dependency.py security_dependency_verdict` releases the hold; `test_security_audit_consolidated_followup_falls_back_to_highest_closed_predecessor` does not cover the same-file case.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:line 3554 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `- Follow-up mode: consolidated (<k> findings in one issue)` is printed whenever `consolidate_active` is true, even if `planned_followups` is empty.
  WHY: On the all-deduped consolidated retry path, the tracker shows "consolidated (0 findings in one issue)" next to "New follow-up issues planned this run: 0"; this is contradictory, but only humans read the line.

- scripts/security_audit.sh:3766, 3793-3799 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

  WHY: If the higher-numbered predecessor is indexed first, the consolidated issue can depend on a lower one closed with ai:merged while the higher one is closed without it, and the follow-up is released too early.
